### 6 Electrochemistry - Multiple Choice: Easy

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-easy-q1 data-answer="B"}
### Question 1 · Oxidation and reduction definitions · 1.6 Choice Easy Q1

Which row correctly describes oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer and changes in oxidation state?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Oxidation gains electrons and increases oxidation state; reduction loses electrons and decreases oxidation state.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Oxidation loses electrons and increases oxidation state; reduction gains electrons and decreases oxidation state.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Oxidation loses electrons and decreases oxidation state; reduction loses electrons and increases oxidation state.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Oxidation gains electrons and decreases oxidation state; reduction gains electrons and increases oxidation state.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> Oxidation is loss of electrons and an increase in oxidation number; reduction is gain of electrons and a decrease.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-easy-q2 data-answer="D"}
### Question 2 · Oxidation state of magnesium sulfate · 1.6 Choice Easy Q2

What is the oxidation state of $\ce{MgSO4}$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$-2$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$+2$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$+7$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$0$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> A neutral compound has an overall oxidation state of zero: $+2+6+4(-2)=0$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-easy-q3 data-answer="D"}
### Question 3 · Common oxidation numbers · 1.6 Choice Easy Q3

Which row describes the most common oxidation numbers of fluorine, oxygen and hydrogen in compounds?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>F $+7$, O $-1$, H $+1$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>F $+4$, O $+2$, H $+1$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>F $-1$, O $+1$, H $-1$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>F $-1$, O $-2$, H $+1$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> Fluorine is $-1$, oxygen is usually $-2$ and hydrogen is usually $+1$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-easy-q4 data-answer="A"}
### Question 4 · Chlorate disproportionation · 1.6 Choice Easy Q4

Chlorate(I) ions decompose on heating. Which row gives the oxidation states of chlorine in $\ce{ClO^-}$, $\ce{ClO3^-}$ and $\ce{Cl^-}$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$+1$, $+5$, $-1$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$+1$, $+3$, $+1$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$-1$, $+5$, $-1$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$-1$, $+3$, $+1$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> In $\ce{ClO^-}$ chlorine is $+1$; in $\ce{ClO3^-}$ it is $+5$; and in $\ce{Cl^-}$ it is $-1$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-easy-q5 data-answer="A"}
### Question 5 · Halogen displacement · 1.6 Choice Easy Q5

A student added a solution of iodine to a solution of sodium bromide. Which statement correctly describes what happens?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>No reaction occurs.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>The bromide ions are oxidised.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>The iodine atoms are oxidised.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Both bromide and iodide ions change oxidation state.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Iodine is below bromine in Group 17 and is not a strong enough oxidising agent to oxidise bromide ions.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-easy-q6 data-answer="D"}
### Question 6 · Change in nitrogen oxidation number · 1.6 Choice Easy Q6

In which reaction is the change in oxidation number for nitrogen the smallest?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$\ce{N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{3Mg + N2 -> Mg3N2}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$\ce{4NH3 + 5O2 -> 4NO + 6H2O}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$\ce{2NO + O2 -> 2NO2}$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> Nitrogen changes from $+2$ in $\ce{NO}$ to $+4$ in $\ce{NO2}$, a change of only 2.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-easy-q7 data-answer="C"}
### Question 7 · Oxidation numbers in complex ions · 1.6 Choice Easy Q7

In the compound $\ce{[ICl2]+[SbCl6]-}$, the oxidation number of chlorine is $-1$. What are the oxidation numbers of I and Sb?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>I $+1$, Sb $+5$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>I $+1$, Sb $+7$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>I $+3$, Sb $+5$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>I $+3$, Sb $+7$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> In $\ce{[ICl2]+}$, I is $+3$; in $\ce{[SbCl6]-}$, Sb is $+5$.</p></details>
:::

### 6 Electrochemistry - Multiple Choice: Medium

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-medium-q1 data-answer="A"}
### Question 8 · Balancing chlorine disproportionation · 1.6 Choice Medium Q1

Chlorine and hot aqueous sodium hydroxide react as:

$$\ce{pCl2 + qOH^- -> rCl^- + sClO3^- + tH2O}$$

What are the values of $p$, $r$ and $s$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$p=3$, $r=5$, $s=1$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$p=3$, $r=6$, $s=2$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$p=2$, $r=5$, $s=1$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$p=2$, $r=4$, $s=2$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> The balanced ionic equation is $\ce{3Cl2+6OH^- ->5Cl^-+ClO3^-+3H2O}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-medium-q2 data-answer="C"}
### Question 9 · Chlorine in water · 1.6 Choice Medium Q2

Which statement about Group 17 redox processes is correct?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Bromine can oxidise chloride ions.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Iodide ions are the weakest reducing agents of the first four halide ions.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>In reactions with water, chlorine is both oxidised and reduced.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Fluorine is a weaker oxidising agent than chlorine.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> In water, chlorine disproportionates to chloride and hypochlorous acid.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-medium-q3 data-answer="B"}
### Question 10 · Identifying an oxidising agent · 1.6 Choice Medium Q3

In which reaction is the species in bold acting as an oxidising agent?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$\ce{Cr2O7^{2-}+8H+ +3SO3^{2-}->2Cr^{3+}+4H2O+3SO4^{2-}}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{Mg + Fe^{2+}->Mg^{2+}+Fe}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$\ce{Cl2+2Br^- ->2Cl^-+Br2}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$\ce{Fe2O3+3CO->2Fe+3CO2}$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ oxidises magnesium and is itself reduced to iron.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-medium-q4 data-answer="C"}
### Question 11 · Equal oxidation numbers · 1.6 Choice Medium Q4

In which compound are there two different elements with the same oxidation number?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$\ce{Mg(OH)2}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{Na2SO4}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$\ce{HClO}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$\ce{NH4Cl}$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> In $\ce{HClO}$, H and Cl are both $+1$ while O is $-2$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-medium-q5 data-answer="A"}
### Question 12 · Sulfuric acid and iodide · 1.6 Choice Medium Q5

When sulfuric acid and sodium iodide react, one reaction is:

$$\ce{8NaI + 9H2SO4 -> 8NaHSO4 + 4I2 + H2S + 4H2O}$$

Which species has been oxidised?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$\ce{I^-}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{SO4^{2-}}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$\ce{Na+}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$\ce{H+}$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Iodide changes from $-1$ to $0$ in $\ce{I2}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-medium-q6 data-answer="D"}
### Question 13 · Titanium dioxide redox analysis · 1.6 Choice Medium Q6

In the reaction used to determine titanium dioxide in an ore, which element increases in oxidation number?

$$\ce{3TiO2 + 4BrF5 -> 3TiF4 + 2Br2 + 3O2}$$

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Fluorine</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Bromine</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Titanium</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Oxygen</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> Oxygen changes from $-2$ in $\ce{TiO2}$ to $0$ in $\ce{O2}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-medium-q7 data-answer="A"}
### Question 14 · Hydrogen as an oxidising agent · 1.6 Choice Medium Q7

In which reaction does hydrogen behave as an oxidising agent?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$\ce{2Na + H2 -> 2NaH}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$\ce{H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$\ce{C2H4 + H2 -> C2H6}$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Hydrogen is reduced from $0$ to $-1$ in $\ce{NaH}$, so it acts as the oxidising agent.</p></details>
:::

### 6 Electrochemistry - Multiple Choice: Hard

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-hard-q1 data-answer="A"}
### Question 15 · Ammonium nitrate decomposition · 1.6 Choice Hard Q1

When heated, ammonium nitrate decomposes:

$$\ce{NH4NO3 -> N2O + 2H2O}$$

The nitrogen atoms in $\ce{NH4NO3}$ have different oxidation numbers. What are their changes in oxidation number?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$+4, -4$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$-2, -4$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$+4, -6$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$+2, +6$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Nitrogen changes from $-3$ in $\ce{NH4+}$ to $+1$ in $\ce{N2O}$, and from $+5$ in $\ce{NO3-}$ to $+1$: changes are $+4$ and $-4$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-hard-q2 data-answer="C"}
### Question 16 · Disproportionation of HIO · 1.6 Choice Hard Q2

The acid $\ce{HIO}$ disproportionates in aqueous solution:

$$\ce{qHIO -> rI2 + sHIO3 + tH2O}$$

The equation is balanced using oxidation numbers. What are the values of $r$ and $s$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$r=4$, $s=2$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$r=4$, $s=1$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$r=2$, $s=1$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$r=1$, $s=2$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> The lowest whole-number equation is $\ce{5HIO -> 2I2 + HIO3 + 2H2O}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-hard-q3 data-answer="B"}
### Question 17 · Sulfur dioxide titration with iodine · 1.6 Choice Hard Q3

In winemaking, sulfur dioxide is titrated with iodine. What is the change in oxidation number of sulfur in this reaction?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$+2$ to $+6$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$+4$ to $+6$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$+2$ to $+4$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$+4$ to $+5$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> Sulfur in $\ce{SO2}$ is $+4$ and is oxidised to $+6$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-hard-q4 data-answer="C"}
### Question 18 · Vanadium and thiosulfate · 1.6 Choice Hard Q4

Using the redox potentials in the original question page, what is the lowest possible oxidation number to which vanadium(V) can be reduced by thiosulfate ions?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$+2$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$+3$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$+4$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$+5$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Only the $\ce{VO2+ / VO^{2+}}$ to $\ce{VO^{2+}}$ step gives a positive emf with thiosulfate, so the final vanadium oxidation state is $+4$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-hard-q5 data-answer="D"}
### Question 19 · Oxidation of chlorine to chlorate(V) · 1.6 Choice Hard Q5

Which reagent and conditions are necessary to oxidise elemental chlorine into a compound containing chlorine in oxidation state $+5$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Concentrated sulfuric acid at room temperature</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{AgNO3(aq)}$ followed by $\ce{NH3(aq)}$ at room temperature</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Cold dilute $\ce{NaOH(aq)}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Hot concentrated $\ce{NaOH(aq)}$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> Hot concentrated alkali gives chlorate(V), $\ce{ClO3^-}$, in which chlorine is $+5$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #electrochemistry-choice-hard-q6 data-answer="B"}
### Question 20 · Sulfuric acid and sodium halides · 1.6 Choice Hard Q6

Concentrated phosphoric acid gives a colourless acidic gas with sodium chloride and sodium iodide. Concentrated sulfuric acid gives a colourless acidic gas with sodium chloride but purple vapour with sodium iodide. Which deduction can be made?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Concentrated sulfuric acid is a stronger oxidising agent than chlorine.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Concentrated sulfuric acid is a stronger oxidising agent than iodine.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Concentrated phosphoric acid is a stronger oxidising agent than iodine.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Concentrated phosphoric acid is a stronger oxidising agent than concentrated sulfuric acid.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> Sulfuric acid oxidises iodide to iodine, whereas phosphoric acid does not; sulfuric acid is therefore the stronger oxidising agent than iodine in this comparison.</p></details>
:::
